text.title: Post Migration Cleanup Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete cleanup checklist for an orders-service schema migration (three flags deleted, one shim retained with a date and counter, snapshot and 41-repository scan before the drop, EUR 432 a month of infrastructure removed, one deferred item with a ticket), with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad checklist (two-day parity, flag frozen, DROP in the code PR, no snapshot) showing what the validator and the reviewer reject.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: orders-service moved from the `orders_v1` Postgres schema and `/v1/orders` endpoint to `orders_v2` and `/v2/orders`. Cutover to 100% traffic happened on 2026-04-01. The team runs two-week sprints. The mobile app below version 4.12 (2.1% of sessions) still calls `/v1/orders`, which a proxy shim forwards to v2. A reconciliation job compares the two schemas nightly.

example.title: orders_v1 to orders_v2 cleanup
example.note: The parity window starts two days after cutover and runs eight days so that it contains a Sunday night, when the invoicing batch runs; `cleanup_deadline` is 14 days (one sprint) after the window closes (r-cleanup-deadline-from-cutover, r-dual-write-retired-after-parity).

The legacy write is gone by PR #8812, which also deletes the `orders.dual_write` key: the flag and the branch it guarded disappear in the same change, and the reconciliation report it cites shows zero mismatches on all eight days (r-dual-write-retired-after-parity, r-migration-flags-removed-from-code).

`orders_v1_reads_total` read zero for nine days including the month-start batch on 2026-04-01 to 04-03; the Grafana link is the evidence, and the read code went in a separate PR from the write deletion so each can be bisected (r-legacy-read-path-deleted-at-zero-traffic).

The proxy shim is `retained` because 2.1% of sessions are an old mobile build: it has a named consumer, a removal date and a counter labelled by client. The column alias had no consumer and no counter, so it was deleted in this cleanup rather than deferred (r-compat-shims-listed-with-expiry).

The DROP is PR #8830, separate from #8812 and #8820; the dump's retention date is after the next quarterly review, and the scan ran across 41 repositories via code search plus the slow-query log with zero hits (r-legacy-schema-dropped-after-backup-and-reference-scan).

The DNS record is the one resource still running, with the shim as the reason and the shim's removal date as its end date; EUR 432 a month is recorded as removed. The alert on v1 write errors is deleted, not muted, so it cannot page on a missing metric (r-alerts-dashboards-and-infra-decommissioned).

The one undone item is in `deferred_items` with a ticket and Dana's name; the checklist waits for Kim to read the snapshot URL and the scan result before #8830 merges (r-cleanup-deadline-from-cutover, human checkpoint).

example.title: What the validator and the reviewer reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.migration.parity_window.days: 2 violates minimum=7`, `$.migration.parity_window.includes_full_weekly_cycle: must equal True, got False`, `$.migration.delivery_cycle_days: 90 violates maximum=30`, `$.dual_write.consecutive_days_zero_mismatch: 2 violates minimum=7`, `$.dual_write.mismatches: must equal 0, got 17`, `$.dual_write.legacy_write_removed_by: must equal 'code_deletion', got 'flag_set_false'`, `$.legacy_read_path.zero_for_days: 0 violates minimum=7`, `$.legacy_read_path.includes_batch_window: must equal True, got False`, `$.flags[0].key_deleted_from_flag_service: must equal True, got False`, `$.flags[0].branches_collapsed: must equal True, got False`, `$.shims[0].consumers: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.shims[0]: matches none of anyOf`, `$.schema_drop.separate_change_from_code_deletion: must equal True, got False`, `$.schema_drop.snapshot.url: length 4 below minLength=5`, `$.schema_drop.reference_scan.query_log_searched: must equal True, got False`, `$.schema_drop.reference_scan.hits: must equal 0, got 3`, `$.docs.hits_after_outside_archive: must equal 0, got 9`, `$.infrastructure[0].reason: missing required field`, `$.infrastructure[0].end_date: missing required field`, `$.review.drop_or_decommission_executed_by_agent: must equal False, got True`, `$.review.reviewer: missing required field`, `$.review.reviewer_read_snapshot_and_scan_on: missing required field`.

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: the DROP is in the same PR as the code deletion (#8812), so a rollback of the code cannot restore the data (r-legacy-schema-dropped-after-backup-and-reference-scan); `orders.read_from_v2` and `orders.v2_shadow_compare` are not listed at all, so two flags survive unaccounted (r-migration-flags-removed-from-code); an empty `observability` list for a service with a known write-error alert means that alert will page on a metric that no longer exists (r-alerts-dashboards-and-infra-decommissioned).
